_README: Copy to athlete/constants.json at the END of intake, not before — see the warning in SETUP.md §2 and the one in skills/intake/SKILL.md. Every athlete-specific number the code needs lives here; nothing in scripts/ or src/ may hardcode a value about the athlete (docs/INVARIANTS.md X-11). The validator requires the fields marked REQUIRED and will fail the build without them. Fill only what this athlete's domains actually need: a key nobody's goals need is a chore the coach invented (CLAUDE.md §1.1), and an unused section is better deleted than filled with a plausible number.

athlete._pronouns_note: The athlete's own, asked for at intake. they/them is the default until they say otherwise — never inferred from a name.
athlete._sex_REQUIRED: "male" or "female". Input to the Mifflin-St Jeor RMR equation ONLY: male adds +5, female subtracts 161 — a 166 kcal/day difference that is invisible on screen if wrong. It is used for nothing else. If no domain needs energy expenditure, it still must be set for the validator; the number simply goes unused.
athlete._dob_REQUIRED: YYYY-MM. Year-month is enough — age moves RMR by 5 kcal/year, so day precision would be false precision. Age is derived, never stored, so it cannot go stale.
athlete._timezone_note: An IANA zone, and it must be the ATHLETE's. Every row's date is derived from it (data/METHOD.md rule 6); the coaching session runs UTC, so leaving someone else's zone here silently mis-dates every evening entry.

baseline._comment: Set once, at intake, from the protocol in skills/intake Session 6. weightLb is REQUIRED by the validator even on charts with no body-composition domain — RMR needs it.

_provenance._comment: REQUIRED once this file exists: one entry per real key above, checked by scripts/test-provenance.mjs. Vocabulary and rules are in data/METHOD.md under 'Provenance'. Shape: { "class": "athlete-stated|athlete-confirmed|coach-proposed-unconfirmed|derived|external", "asOf": "YYYY-MM-DD", "source": "where the reasoning is written down", "note": "whose number this is, in prose" } — plus "quote" or "measured" for the athlete- classes, and "inputs" for derived. Never add a marker to a value you did not trace; an unmarked value is honest, a wrongly-marked one is not.

plan._comment: Current phase parameters. Only fill what this athlete's domains actually need — a chart with no energy domain does not need a calorie budget, and inventing one is the failure CLAUDE.md §1.1 exists to prevent. estMaintenanceKcal and proteinFloorG are validator-required. Optional keys the code reads if present, and ignores if absent: fatTargetG and fibreTargetG (written into each generated targets.csv row), weeklyAlcoholKcalBudget (subtracted from weeklyKcalBudget to give the food allowance — it sits INSIDE the calorie budget, never on top of it).

kcalByWeekday._comment: REQUIRED wherever a calorie target exists, and the reason it is a weekday map rather than one daily figure is that the unevenness is usually the plan — a bigger day parked where the athlete actually wants it. scripts/generate-targets.mjs writes one targets.csv row per day from this and EXITS NON-ZERO on any weekday it has no entry for, because a day without a target is the failure CLAUDE.md §0.3 and data/METHOD.md both call out by name. Seven entries, keyed exactly: Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun — CAPITALISED and three letters, because that is what every weekday lookup in the code produces. Seven right numbers under seven wrong names is a chart where every single day has no target, and validate-data.mjs now checks the KEYS rather than counting them. The validator additionally checks they sum to weeklyKcalBudget — a total that disagrees with its parts is a record contradicting itself. No example figures are given here on purpose: a calorie target is a decision about a person, and a plausible-looking placeholder is how one gets inherited. If this chart has no energy domain, delete this key and the daily-rollover workflow with it.

plan._trend_note: How the anchored trend is measured, and both are optional — 3 and 10 are the shipped defaults and are right for a chart weighed most mornings. `trendWindowSize` is how many readings each end of the comparison averages; `trendLagDays` is how far apart the two ends sit. A chart measuring something weekly rather than daily wants a larger lag (a 10-day gap holds one reading either side, so every figure it produces is marked not-firm); a chart measuring twice a day may want a larger window. They govern the LEVEL and the RATE together, which is the point of the estimator — see anchoredTrend in scripts/lib/aggregate.mjs. Neither changes what is measured, so neither needs a provenance marker: they are how this chart reads its own record, not a claim about the athlete.
plan._max_rate_note: CLAUDE.md §5.2 hard floor. Do not raise it.
plan._adherenceRoutingPct_note: Not the athlete's number and not the coach's — it is CLAUDE.md §7's routing rule, so it ships filled in and its provenance class is `external`. Below this, a week routes to the adherence agent instead of the domain specialists, because a plan that is not being followed is not a programming problem. scripts/test-single-home.mjs checks that every document stating this figure states the same one; leave the value here and cite the key elsewhere rather than retyping 80.
plan._movement_note: THE MOVEMENT SLOT IN THE BURN MODEL, AND EVERY CHART FILLS IT ONE OF TWO WAYS. `stepFeed` names the automation that writes data/steps.csv — today that is the iOS Shortcut behind .github/workflows/log-steps.yml, so the value is "apple-health-shortcut". It is a NAME rather than true/false so a second writer added later is a new value, not a new branch. Leave it out on a chart with no wearable: that is the common configuration, it is not a lesser one, and check-steps.yml then stops mailing a failure every morning about a file nothing writes. `movementOutsideExerciseLevel` is the other filling — how much this athlete moves on an ordinary day OUTSIDE deliberate exercise, one of: seated | light | active | on-feet (descriptions in scripts/lib/movement.mjs, and skills/intake asks the question). OUTSIDE DELIBERATE EXERCISE IS NOT PHRASING: a walk they chose to go on is logged as a session and priced as one, so a level that also covered it would count that walk twice. Set exactly one of the two — validate-data.mjs rejects both together, because the feed already counts what the level describes. A chart that sets NEITHER runs on the shipped default level, marked coach-proposed-unconfirmed, which is a question waiting to be answered rather than a number filed as the athlete's. The kcal/day figure itself is DERIVED from the level and stored nowhere; a second copy in this file could disagree with the ledger.

_movement_example._comment: Copy ONE of these two into plan, never both. Shown as an example rather than shipped live because an empty stepFeed is not a declaration and a provenance marker on one would be recording an answer nobody gave — whereas a chart that HAS a feed states it, and then owes a marker like any other value.

_provenance._comment: REQUIRED once this file exists — see baseline._provenance above for the shape. A target the athlete is asked to hit is `coach-proposed-unconfirmed` until they have ruled on it in words about that number; adherence is not confirmation. Never invent a marker to clear the check, and never delete a value to make one go away. The two entries below ship filled in because their provenance is a fact about this system rather than about any athlete — they are also the worked example of the shape.

maxRatePctBwPerWk.source: CLAUDE.md §5.2, 'No sustained loss rate above 1.0% of bodyweight per week'
maxRatePctBwPerWk.note: The charter's safety floor, not this athlete's preference and not the coach's judgement. It ships with the template at 1.0 and is enforced against the athlete's own instruction; it is not negotiable downward by either party.

_movementOutsideExerciseLevel_example.quote: <their words about an ordinary day — not about exercise>
_movementOutsideExerciseLevel_example.source: <the intake session or log where they said it>
_movementOutsideExerciseLevel_example.note: Their own description. The kcal figure it prices at is the coach's arithmetic over it and is `derived`, which is why it is not stored: data/METHOD.md rule 5 is explicit that a maintenance-shaped figure is derived or external even though the coach chose its coefficients. If nobody has answered yet, the shipped default applies and its marker is `coach-proposed-unconfirmed` with the date it started standing in.

adherenceRoutingPct.source: CLAUDE.md §7, 'Route to adherence whenever completion falls below 80% for a week'
adherenceRoutingPct.note: The charter's routing rule. Nobody on this chart chose 80 — it ships with the template, and every document that states the figure is checked against this key by scripts/test-single-home.mjs so the four copies cannot drift apart.

triggers._comment: Machine-readable mirror of the trigger values in athlete/goals.md, so the dashboard can draw reference lines and the findings layer can fire. goals.md is authoritative for the reasoning; if the two disagree, goals.md wins and this is the bug. ONLY the keys named below are recognised — scripts/lib/findings.mjs and src/app/page.tsx read them by name, so a trigger invented under a different key renders nowhere and fires never. Every one is optional; a chart that measures none of these carries none of them. If this athlete's domains need a trigger with no key here, it needs code, not a new key — raise it rather than writing one that silently does nothing.

_recognised.waistTriggerIn: Goal line on the waist chart; fires a finding at or past it.
_recognised.waistWorkingBaselineIn: Reference line the waist trend is read against.
_recognised.weightCheckpointLb: A review checkpoint — fires a finding at or past it. Not a goal and not a floor.
_recognised.weightFloorLb: The deficit stops here regardless of anything else. Fires below it.

_provenance._comment: REQUIRED once this file exists — see baseline._provenance above. A threshold the athlete has not ruled on is `coach-proposed-unconfirmed`, and it stays live and marked rather than being deleted. Anything clinical belongs to their doctor: route it, never pick a number to close a gap.

domains._comment: The athlete/goals.md domain headings, VERBATIM, keyed by the role the code needs to name one for. This is the machine-readable pointer; goals.md holds the reasoning and the ranking. Without it, findings render with no domain label — which is honest, and is why there is no default: a default would be another chart's domain wearing this one's name. Roles the code asks for: `energyDeficit` (the domain a calorie deficit serves) and `health`. A TRAINING domain needs no role here — every session type already declares the domain it serves, required and validated, in sessionTypes.<type>.domain, and a finding about a session reads it from there. Add a key only when this chart actually has that domain.

sessionTypes._comment: WHAT THIS ATHLETE DOES, and what each activity costs, counts for, and serves. The list is the athlete's, not the system's: scripts/lib/schema.mjs derives training.csv's `type` enum from these keys, scripts/lib/athlete.mjs derives the MET table and the sessions-floor set, and the dashboard's /log form offers exactly these. AN ACTIVITY THAT IS NOT REGISTERED CAN ONLY BE LOGGED AS `other`, WHICH COUNTS TOWARD NOTHING — so an athlete who runs, and whose chart never registered running, trains six days a week and is invisible to the adherence count (audit F-15). `rest` and `other` are supplied by scripts/lib/athlete.mjs to every chart; do not register them, the validator rejects it. Required per entry: met (0-25), countsTowardFloor (true|false), domain (the goals.md heading it serves). Optional: note, metByIntensity ({light,moderate,hard} — used when a session logs its own minute split, so a long easy session is not priced at its hardest tier), energyCountedIn (name another column whose data already includes this activity's energy — then met MUST be 0, or it is counted twice), loading (true|false — DID THIS TIRE YOU OUT. A third question, not a restatement of the other two: countsTowardFloor asks whether it earns credit against the sessions/week floor, met asks whether it burns calories, and real registries come apart on all three. A rehabilitation or mobility block can load genuinely while deliberately earning no floor credit; a walking type priced at a real MET — which is correct on a chart with NO step feed, where nothing else counts that movement — may still be a rest day. Omit it and it defaults to `met > 0 and no energyCountedIn`, which is right for most entries; set it only where that default is wrong. It feeds the consecutive-loading-days count that tells a coach how hard the last few days have been), standingDurationMin (minutes — ONLY for a type that always runs the same length, such as a short daily block or a fixed-length class. It lets the ledger cost a session that was performed but not timed at the figure the forward view already uses, instead of estimating it from set count. Omit it for anything whose length actually varies, which is most activities: a wrong standing duration is worse than a reconstructed one, because it does not declare itself an estimate).

<a short block that always runs the same.note: The third entry exists to show what `standingDurationMin` is for. Because this always takes the same time, a row logged without a duration can be costed at the declared figure rather than estimated — and the ledger and the forward view then agree about it.

<a walking type, on a chart with no step.note: The second entry exists to show the ONE case `loading` is for. With no step feed nothing else counts this movement, so it is priced as a session at a real MET — and the default would then call it loading and read a week of walks as a week with no rest day.

program._comment: The current block's weekly skeleton, so /today can show the planned session without waiting for a coaching session to hand-write a training.csv row. A real training.csv row ALWAYS wins over this. Rationale, exercise detail and autoregulation live in program/current-block.md; this is only the machine-readable outline, and a chart with no training domain does not need it at all. `weeklyTemplate` is keyed Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun — capitalised, three letters, same as plan.kcalByWeekday and for the same reason: `planDay()` looks the day up with that key, and a lower-cased map silently resolves to no session at all; `dailyBlockType` names which registry type the `Daily` prescription block is, and is how the forward view prices it — its minutes and its MET both come from that type's registry entry, so `sessionTypes.<type>.standingDurationMin` is the ONE place the block's length is written and the ledger and the forecast cannot disagree about it. Omit both where the chart prescribes no daily block. `setRestSec` is optional and overrides the shipped 70-second default used to reconstruct the duration of a session that was performed but not timed — `skills/intake` asks whether 70 is right, and until somebody answers it stays marked coach-proposed. A session type that always runs the same length declares that on the TYPE, as `sessionTypes.<type>.standingDurationMin`, not here: it is a property of the activity rather than of the current block. `conditioningMenu` is the list of non-lifting-day options a coach may be handed, as the session NAMES their prescription rows use in data/prescriptions.csv — names only, because the contents, the selection rules and the custom-build hatch live in the menu document (copy library/optional/program/conditioning-menu.md into program/ and fill it in). scripts/check-suspensions.mjs holds EVERY name here to the active block's suspension list, not just the one today's weekday template happens to name, so an option built on a movement the block has since taken out fails the build instead of being proposed; and skills/library/session-recommendation reads it to know what it may choose from. Omit it entirely on a chart with no menu — that is a normal chart, not an incomplete one, because building a session from the last three days is a complete answer. A custom session built for one day does NOT go here: it goes in prescriptions.csv under its own name, and earns a place here only if it recurs.

_example.dailyBlockType: <a registry key from sessionTypes, or omit>
conditioningMenu: <a session name, exactly as data/prescriptions.csv writes it>

events._comment: Dated things worth counting down to: a trip, a procedure, an event the plan is built around.

copy._comment: Sentences the dashboard renders that are about THIS athlete — their measurement history, their block, their protocol. One of the four homes for athlete-specific language (scripts/check-no-athlete-leak.mjs), and it exists because shared components used to carry these as string literals, so every new chart inherited the previous athlete's tile labels and caveats (audit F-31). Every key is optional: a page with no entry renders a generic sentence or renders nothing, and that is a correct chart rather than a gap. NOTHING HERE MAY CARRY A NUMBER that has a home elsewhere — scripts/test-single-home.mjs checks prose figures against this file, and this key is prose. Keys the pages read: waistTileLabel, waistCardTitle, waistCardCaption, bodyFormCaption, templateFlexNote.

metrics._comment: Registry for anything tracked in data/metrics.csv — the long-format file for measures the fixed columns of body.csv don't cover. This is where a symptom count, a medication, a lab value or a device reading goes, in the athlete's own vocabulary, so a new chart never needs code edited to record a new thing. Every entry must name its unit, its direction (up|down = which way is progress), and the goals.md domain it serves. The validator rejects an entry with no domain, because a metric no domain needs is a chore the coach invented. Two more per entry decide how the coach TREATS it, and both have defaults so an existing registry keeps working: `feed` is `manual` or `automated` — whether anything writes this without the athlete saying it — and `cadence` is `daily`, `episodic` or `lab`. They exist because a metric that only exists when somebody reports it has to be asked for, and one a device writes must never be asked for: CLAUDE.md §0.2 states that rule once, over this registry, so it names no metric and needs no edit when a chart tracks a different thing. The defaults are `manual` and `episodic` — the safe pair, because an episodic metric is never chased, so a wrong default costs a question nobody asks rather than a daily nag about something a device already recorded.
